== Problem ==

Let <imath>n</imath> be the least prime number that can be written as the sum of <imath>5</imath> distinct prime numbers. What is the sum of the digits of <imath>n</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }5\qquad\textbf{(B) }7\qquad\textbf{(C) }8\qquad\textbf{(D) }10\qquad\textbf{(E) }13</imath>

== Solution 1==
Let the requested sum be <imath>S.</imath> Recall that <imath>2</imath> is the only even (and the smallest) prime, so <imath>S</imath> is odd. It follows that the five distinct primes are all odd. The first few odd primes are <imath>3,5,7,11,13,17,19,\ldots.</imath> We conclude that <imath>S>3+5+7+11+13=39,</imath> as <imath>39</imath> is a composite. The next possible value of <imath>S</imath> is <imath>3+5+7+11+17=43,</imath> which is a prime. Therefore, we have <imath>S=43,</imath> and the sum of its digits is <imath>4+3=\boxed{\textbf{(B) }7}.</imath>

~MRENTHUSIASM

== Solution 2 ==
We notice that the minimum possible value of the sum of <imath>5</imath> odd distinct primes is <imath>3 + 5 + 7 + 11 + 13 = 39</imath>, which is not a prime. The smallest prime greater than that is <imath>41</imath>. However, this cannot be written as the sum of <imath>5</imath> distinct primes, since <imath>15</imath> is not prime. However, <imath>43</imath> can be written as <imath>3 + 5 + 7 + 11 + 17 = 43</imath>, so the answer is <imath>4 + 3 = \boxed{\textbf{(B) }7}</imath> 

~andliu766
